sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a trauma victim shows a broad hepatic laceration with foci of active bleeding and hemoperitoneum . Note adjacent rib fractures .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-01

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT in a patient with a falling hematocrit following liver biopsy shows high-density blood in a linear tract deep within the liver , representing the biopsy site and depth. Also note the extension as a subcapsular hematoma, the lentiform collection lateral to the liver .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-02

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows a deep linear focus of hyperdensity and a subcapsular collection of similar appearance. The hematoma was due to a percutaneous liver biopsy.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-03

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a young woman shows a hypervascular mass in the right lobe with a large, spontaneous subcapsular hematoma .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-04

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT in a young woman with acute pain shows a mass in the lateral segment with high-attenuation material centrally due to an acute hematoma.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-05

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 MR in a young woman shows a hepatic mass containing several hyperintense foci that represent hemorrhage. The foci were hyperintense on T2 as well, distinguishing hemorrhage from fat as the etiology.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-06

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 FS MR shows peripheral foci of hyperintensity on T1 that remained hyperintense on T2, indicating hemorrhage. This was hepatic adenoma.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-07

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Arterial-phase CECT in a man with cirrhosis and sudden right upper quadrant (RUQ) pain shows tumor vessels within a poorly defined, hypervascular mass . Ascites and a sentinel clot overlying the hepatic mass are seen. Spontaneous rupture of hepatocellular carcinoma was the etiology.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-08

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Arterial-phase CECT in the same patient shows part of the hypervascular mass , as well as the ascites and sentinel clot overlying the site of the capsular rupture. A catheter angiogram confirmed bleeding hepatocellular carcinoma. It was treated with coil embolization.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-09

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT in a 60-year-old man with alcoholic liver disease and sudden RUQ pain shows a hyperdense sentinel clot within and around the liver as well as a spherical hepatic mass .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-10

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal CECT in a woman with cirrhosis and sudden RUQ pain shows a heterogeneous, encapsulated mass that was hyperdense on arterial phase. There is generalized ascites but also a sentinel clot over the mass, indicating the source of bleeding.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-11

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a large mass with a thin wall, characteristic of a simple cyst. Within the cyst is a heterogeneous focus of higher attenuation , suggestive of acute hemorrhage. Other sections showed hemorrhagic ascites.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-12

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Grayscale ultrasound shows a hepatic cyst containing a heterogeneous organizing hematoma with fibrin strands .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-13

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial FS T2 MR shows a large, complex cystic mass with dependent settling of material that is hypointense on T2, indicating subacute hemorrhage.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-14

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 GRE opposed-phase MR shows many cysts within an enlarged liver. Many of the cysts are of water intensity (dark on this T1), while others are bright, due to hemorrhage.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-15

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows signs of coagulopathic hemorrhage, including the hematocrit sign , active bleeding , and multiple sites of bleeding, including hepatic and renal .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-16

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a patient who was taking anticoagulant medication shows hepatic defects that resemble fracture planes , but there was no history of trauma. A subcapsular hematoma and hemoperitoneum are also shown. All findings resolved with withdrawal of the medication. No underlying hepatic mass or other pathology was found.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-17

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a large metastatic lesion in the liver from a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor with a subcapsular hematoma from spontaneous bleeding.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-18

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a 55-year-old man with melanoma shows metastasis to the liver that is peculiarly heterogeneous and high density, perhaps indicating bleeding within the metastasis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-19

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a patient with metastatic melanoma and acute RUQ pain shows a hepatic mass . Immediately adjacent to this metastasis is a heterogeneous sentinel clot , strongly suggesting bleeding from the metastases. Also noted is an extensive hemoperitoneum with an attenuation of 35 HU.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-20

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a young woman with toxemia and sudden RUQ pain shows a massive subcapsular and perihepatic hematoma , along with active bleeding and heterogeneous enhancement of the hepatic parenchyma .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-21

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a postpartum woman with RUQ pain shows a large, subcapsular hematoma and hepatic infarcts .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-22

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: In this woman with HELLP syndrome and spontaneous bleeding, a selective hepatic arteriogram indirectly shows the subcapsular hematoma as the liver is displaced medially. It also shows multiple foci of active hemorrhage , which were treated with coil embolization.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-23

CORE_EVIDENCE_FILE_BEGIN
CORE_EVIDENCE_STATUS: USED
CORE_SOURCE_BASIS: junzi-shi-core-radiology-a-visual-approach-to.pdf; Gastrointestinal Imaging, Liver section, pp. 105-120, with additional Nuclear and Molecular Imaging liver/spleen scintigraphy coverage around pp. 462-463.
CORE_FACTS_USED:

- HCC progression from regenerative nodule to dysplastic nodule to HCC, with increasing neovascularity; classic arterial enhancement, portal venous/delayed washout, capsule, T2 hyperintensity, possible diffusion restriction, and tumor-in-vein assessment.
- Hepatic adenoma has a relatively high hemorrhage risk; arterial hyperenhancement with iso-/hypoenhancement on portal venous/delayed phases; variable ultrasound appearance; usually photopenic sulfur-colloid appearance and paucity of HIDA uptake; adenomas >5 cm are usually resected.
- Simple hepatic cysts are thin-walled and nonenhancing; ultrasound is anechoic with posterior enhancement and no internal Doppler flow; CT attenuation is 0-20 HU; MRI is low T1/high T2. ADPLD produces innumerable nonenhancing simple hepatic cysts.
- Most hepatic metastases are hypovascular and best appreciated on portal venous CT; metastases are generally T1 hypointense/T2 hyperintense, while blood products or melanin may be T1 hyperintense; ultrasound may show a target sign.
- Core identifies adenoma, HCC, and metastases among hemorrhagic hepatic lesion patterns.
- Core liver-trauma coverage supplies the CT-based AAST liver injury framework, including subcapsular hematoma, laceration depth, vascular injury/active bleeding, intraperitoneal extension, and major hepatic venous injury.
CORE_DERIVED_CARDS:
- HCC CT, MRI, ultrasound/Doppler, sulfur-colloid, tumor-in-vein, clinical-prior, and mechanism cards.
- Hepatic adenoma CT, MRI, ultrasound, nuclear medicine, >5-cm management, clinical-prior, mechanism, and hemorrhage-versus-fat trap cards.
- Hemorrhagic hepatic cyst CT, MRI, ultrasound, and clot-versus-tumor trap cards.
- ADPLD imaging and ADPKD-association cards.
- Hepatic metastasis CT, MRI, ultrasound, and hemorrhagic-metastasis discriminator cards.
- Hepatic trauma CT and AAST liver-injury framework cards.
CORE_LIMITATIONS:
- HELLP-specific hepatic hemorrhage/infarction and coagulopathic hepatic hemorrhage details used in the deck were derived from the RadPrimer/STATdx source package rather than retrieved Core coverage.
- The 35-HU melanoma hemoperitoneum example and the >60-HU general NECT hemorrhage statement were preserved as separate RadPrimer/STATdx contexts rather than generalized.
- Coil embolization and anticoagulant-withdrawal outcomes were retained only as case-specific source statements, not universal management algorithms.
- No external medical literature was used.
CORE_EVIDENCE_FILE_END
